headline: Congress extended federal programs through 2027 that screen newborns and young children for hearing loss and help them get early services.
what_it_does: The law renews funding authority through fiscal year 2027 for hearing screening and early intervention work carried out by three federal agencies: the Health Resources and Services Administration, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders. These efforts support newborns, infants, and young children who are deaf or hard of hearing. The law also requires the Government Accountability Office to study state early hearing detection and intervention programs, including whether some groups have more trouble getting into them.

who_it_affects.group: Newborns, infants, and young children who are deaf or hard of hearing
who_it_affects.how: Federal screening and early intervention support for them is authorized to continue through fiscal year 2027.

who_it_affects.group: Families of young children with possible hearing loss
who_it_affects.how: Programs that test for hearing loss and connect children to services are authorized to keep operating, and the GAO study may point to ways to make access fairer.

who_it_affects.group: State health and early intervention programs
who_it_affects.how: States that run hearing screening and early intervention programs may keep receiving federal support, and they may be reviewed in the GAO study.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 20, 2022; the reauthorized activities run through fiscal year 2027.
